finding.claim: Unauthenticated access to the email-change endpoint: POST /settings/email is decorated with login_optional instead of login_required, so anonymous requests reach set_email(None, ...).
finding.source: Anonymous HTTP POST to /settings/email (routes.py:34-35); login_optional (routes.py:19-23) sets g.uid = session.get('uid') = None without aborting.

trace.note: g.uid = session.get('uid') -> None for anonymous; no abort

finding.guards_checked: login_optional never aborts; change_email has no internal g.uid check; no other middleware visible in repo. Sibling /settings/password correctly uses login_required. set_email is a stub (routes.py:48-49), so real impact depends on out-of-repo implementation.

verdict.guard_found: none. login_optional (routes.py:19-23) assigns g.uid = session.get("uid") (None for anonymous) and never aborts; change_email (routes.py:35-37) has no g.uid check and calls set_email unconditionally. The only file in the directory is routes.py, so there is no app-level before_request or auth middleware. Sibling change_password (routes.py:41-44) correctly uses login_required, which calls abort(401) at routes.py:11-12.
verdict.reason: The anonymous POST to /settings/email reaches set_email(None, "new@example.org") at routes.py:37 because the route is decorated with login_optional (routes.py:35), which never aborts (routes.py:19-23), and nothing else in the repo blocks it. The real impact depends on the out-of-repo set_email, which is a stub at routes.py:48-49, so the finding's severity is unconfirmed even though the reachability is confirmed.

finding.claim: Password change ignores request input and sets a hardcoded password ('hunter2') with no current-password or re-authentication check and no visible CSRF protection, enabling account takeover.
finding.source: Authenticated user POST to /settings/password (routes.py:41-42); request body is never read.

trace.note: login_required checks 'uid' in session, aborts 401 otherwise

finding.guards_checked: Authentication enforced via login_required. No current-password check, no re-auth, no CSRF token/SameSite config visible in repo (CSRF path is conditional on out-of-repo app config). Hardcoded credential value 'hunter2'.

verdict.guard_found: login_required (routes.py:8-16, abort(401) at line 12) enforces a session uid, but it is an authentication check only. No current-password, re-auth, or CSRF check exists in the repo. Nothing blocks set_password(g.uid, "hunter2") at routes.py:44 once a logged-in request arrives. CSRF protection and SameSite cookie settings are not visible in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: routes.py:41-44 sets a fixed "hunter2" value via set_password(g.uid, ...) after login_required (routes.py:11-12) passes, and the request body is ignored. The account-takeover claim does not hold for the in-repo attacker, since an authenticated user can only change their own uid (routes.py:13, 44). Takeover of a victim requires a victim-triggered cross-site POST, and whether that is blocked depends on out-of-repo CSRF/SameSite config, so this cannot be decided from the code available.
